full_judgment:
This Rule arises out of an application challenging the concurrent decision of both the Courts below decreeing a suit for declaring a divorce at the instance of a wife upon a delegated power as illegal and consequently passing a decree for restitution of conjugal rights at the instance of the husband. 

 2. The petitioner, while she was a 1st Year student in the Dacca University in English Department was married with the opposite party on 15th April, 1976. It is represented that the couple and the spouse were married at the marriage registration office avoiding any social function. That the bride and bridegroom were major is not in dispute and that they married without the concurrence of the respective parents is also not in dispute. Thus it is quite clear that the petitioner though a student at the relevant time in the Dacca University married the opposite party out of her free will and choice. It is also not disputed that at the time of the marriage the petitioner's husband had though obtained his graduation degree in pass course but was unemployed and had no establishment of his own. Subsequently the petitioner's husband, however, became employed with the Power Development Board as Labour Welfare Officer and was posted at Shahji Bazar in Sylhet since September, 1976. In such circumstances the petitioner and her husband developed animosity amongst them and consequently the husband instituted a suit for restitution of conjugal rights within one year of their marriage on 6th April, 1977. Upon receipt of the summons in the aforesaid suit from the trial court and during the pendency of such suit, the petitioner herein being the wire exercised her delegated power of divorce against her husband, which is commonly known under the Muslim Personnel Law as Talaq-e-Tawfiz. Such divorce was registered with the marriage registration office on 1st June, 1978 and a notice of the registration of the said Talaqnama was sent to the Mayor of Dacca and to the petitioner's husband. Long after the registration of the Talaqnama the petitioner's husband being the opposite party herein caused the amendment of the plaint of his suit for restitution of conjugal rights by an order dated 18th August, 1978 and it was converted into a suit for declaring the exercise of divorce by way of delegated power as have been done illegally without any lawful authority having no legal effect. The suit however was heard in due course by the trial court when the plaintiff being the husband and his sister's husband and also defendant being the wife deposed before the court and were examined and cross-examined. Consequently the trial court decreed the suit on 28.11.80 declaring the exercise of divorce by delegated power as have been done illegally and directing the restitution of conjugal rights. The lower appellate court also having affirmed such decision of the trial court, the wife naturally moved this court and obtained this Rule under disposal. 

 4. The courts below, it appears, have proceeded upon three grounds for decreeing the plaintiff husband's suit under the amended plaint. Firstly, it has been held that the divorce at the option of the wife by way of the delegated power was illegal since it was not in pursuance of the terms of the Kabinnama Secondly, it has been held that the right of divorce by way of delegated power having been exercised by the wife during the pendency of the suit against her for restitution of conjugal rights, the principle of the common law doctrine of lispendens would be applicable in the present case to justify the annulling of such divorce Thirdly, it has been held that the divorce was bad for lack of service of proper notice upon the husband as contemplated under Family Law Ordinance. 

 8. While decreeing the suit for declaring the act of divorce at the instance of the wife as illegal, the courts below further made a direction for restitution of conjugal rights as a consequential relief. In a suit challenging any marriage or divorce as the case may be by way of any declaratory relief, there cannot be any consequential relief in the nature of restitution of conjugal rights, because a consequential relief must always be enforceable and executable under the law and any direction for restitution of conjugal rights is not capable of being physically enforceable and executable through any process of law. 

 10. Be that as it may, in the foregoing facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated herein before, the impugned judgments of both the courts below decreeing the suit against the present petitioner declaring her act of divorce as illegal and directing restitution of conjugal rights having been held illegal are set aside and Title Suit No. 192 of 1977 before the First Munsif of Dacca is accordingly dismissed. This Rule is made absolute with costs.
